name: copy
reason: Mirror: copyShallow writes the bound-method branch as a new MethodType(f, s), but CPython reaches it through method.__reduce__ (Objects/classobject.c:91-116), which returns getattr(__self__, __func__.__name__), so copy(m) can be a different object or AttributeError, and it has no copyreg.dispatch_table step (:84-86) and no __reduce__ fallback (:92-94); property: CopyShallow pins only the list, tuple and hooked-error/str/Error branches, so a copy that fails on dicts, instances, frozendicts, a succeeding __copy__ or a reduce tuple (never linked to reconShallow) still satisfies it, and the pickle-reduce refutation runs only reconShallow, not copyShallow.

name: deepcopy
reason: Mirror: the model has no copyreg.dispatch_table step (:139-141), cannot express __reduce_ex__ = None falling back to __reduce__ (:143-149), and drops _keep_alive (:161), whose memo[id(memo)] entry a caller-supplied memo and every __deepcopy__(memo) can see; property: no theorem pins the issubclass(cls, type) branch (:132-133), a succeeding __deepcopy__ and its memo entry (:137, :159-160), a reduce string (:153-154) or a raising reductor, so a deepcopy that errors or memoizes wrongly on those paths passes every listed entry.

name: _deepcopy_list
reason: The model allocates y, records memo[id(x)] = y before copying, copies items in order and stops at the first failure (:172-177); DeepcopyMemo (self-list cycle), DeepcopyAliasing ([a, a] gives one new object), DeepcopyListExact and DeepCopyOrder (first item's error wins whatever follows) rule out reversed order, no memo-first and no sharing.

name: _deepcopy_tuple
reason: Copies, the second memo read, then the identity zip (:181-194) are mirrored, and deepcopy memoizes only a new tuple; DeepcopyTupleExact pins the new-tuple and t = ([t],) second-read paths, and the y = x branch is pinned only by corelibs-copy-tuple-identity, which names this function in pyFns but is missing from the row's entry column and should be added.

name: _deepcopy_dict
reason: The model sets memo before the loop, copies value before key (assignment order at :201) and stores through dictSet, which hashes first and keeps the first equal key with the last value as insertdict does (Objects/dictobject.c:2001-2049, :2744-2759); DeepcopyDictExact, DeepcopyDictMerge (first key object, last value) and DeepCopyOrder (value first) fail key-first, append-always and last-key-wins versions; the unhashable-key-copy TypeError is mirrored but not stated for this function, and a key with its own raising __hash__ or __eq__ is outside the stated scope.

name: _deepcopy_frozendict
reason: Copies into a fresh dict through the same deepPairs/dictSet store with no memo entry, then the memo read, then a new frozendict (:206-217); DeepcopyFrozendict pins that the result is always a new object (unlike the tuple), that a memo copy made during recursion wins, and that the first failure propagates.

name: _deepcopy_method
reason: type(x)(x.__func__, deepcopy(x.__self__, memo)) (:221) is mirrored with the function shared and __self__ deep-copied, then memoized by deepcopy; DeepcopyMethod's first conjunct states that exact result for every heap, so a copy of the function or a shared __self__ fails it.

name: _keep_alive
reason: The no-behaviour reason does not apply: the body writes memo[id(memo)] = [..., x] into the memo, which the caller of deepcopy(x, memo) and every __deepcopy__(memo) can see, and which deepcopy(memo, memo) returns at :125-126; it also keeps temporary objects alive so their ids are not reused within one pass, which the model avoids only because its cells are never freed.

name: _reconstruct
reason: Mirror: reconRest calls __setstate__ for a state cell that is None (atom 0, the model's own None per stateStep), skipping the `if state is not None` of :252 (it is checked only inside stateStep), y.__dict__.update(state) accepts only a dict cell where CPython takes any mapping or iterable of pairs, and is evaluated after the state rather than before (an empty state on a y without __dict__ is AttributeError in CPython and ok in the model), and listiter/dictiter are plain lists that cannot raise; property: ReconstructSteps' third conjunct and ReconRestItems' fifth and sixth claim __setstate__ runs (or its error propagates) for every st, including None, which is false for CPython when the reduce state is None.

name: replace
reason: replaceOp takes the already-computed result of func(obj, **changes) as an Option (Py β), so it does not mirror the obj.__class__ lookup, getattr(cls, '__replace__', None) (including an explicit None), or the call with changes (:296-300); the two conjuncts are rfl on that one-line match, which any function returning its argument or a TypeError also satisfies.
